reason: Compared the complete source definition labelled def:shift (the reversal definition) with SM.reversal_definition, SM.reversal and its actual cyclic-quotient construction. The representative map is exactly reversal P i=P(2-i), with index arithmetic in ZMod n, and the theorem explicitly proves that label 1 retains P 1. This matches the source one-based convention, including residue zero representing the final vertex, rather than using the different map i maps to -i or reversing around a different base vertex. The formula reverses cyclic traversal: the supporting edge identity is edge(reversal P,i)=-edge(P,1-i), and the supporting turn identity is turn(reversal P,i)=-turn(P,2-i), both with the correct orientation and offsets. The exact conjugacy reversal(shift a P)=shift(-a)(reversal P) proves the source's 'commutes with the shift up to a shift.' reversal_respects_cyclic then supplies well-definedness to Quotient.map on the existing Polygon n hn quotient, and polygonReversal_mk identifies its value on every representative with the class of that representative's actual reversal. The cyclic equivalence relation has not been enlarged to identify a polygon with its reversal. Involution is proved for the quotient map, as an additional valid property, without replacing reversal by a trivial identity. All raw tuples on the inherited n>=3 domain are included; no genericity, nonzero edge, regularity or orientation-invariance hypothesis is added. Degenerate or specially symmetric tuples may of course have a reversal in their own cyclic orbit, but no universal distinction or universal cyclic equivalence is asserted. The source rho notation denotes this same reversal map, so no separate operation is missing. The text's caution that later laws are not automatically reversal-invariant is respected: the aggregate asserts the source operation and its descent plus concrete sign-changing edge/turn formulas, not invariance of the corner laws or any later theorem. The audited semantic dependency inventory binds reversal, polygonReversal, the actual Polygon/cyclicSetoid/shift definitions and the geometric edge/turn meanings. All source clauses are covered. This is one original definition row; the supporting involution, edge and turn lemmas are not additional original claims.
